# quire.lock and the cache

## quire.lock

`quire.lock` records the exact commit of every git dependency, including
dependencies of dependencies:

```toml
# This file is generated by quire. Do not edit it by hand.
version = 1

[[package]]
name = "lab-macros"
source = "git+https://github.com/mylab/lab-macros?tag=v1.2"
rev = "57179c1642b2e33dd7c19e6fac0f1463e5684e18"
```

- Commit it. Everyone who builds the project then uses the same revisions.
- It is created the first time a project has a git dependency, and only
  rewritten when the dependencies change. Entries for removed dependencies are
  dropped.
- Changing a dependency's `tag`, `branch` or `rev` changes its `source`, so it
  is resolved again.
- `quire update` moves entries to the newest allowed commit. `--locked` makes
  any change an error.

Path and distribution dependencies aren't locked: a path is already exact, and
distribution packages come from your TeX installation.

## The cache: `~/.quire`

Git dependencies are cached once per machine and shared between projects:

```text
~/.quire/
├── .package-cache                       # lock file, see below
└── git/
    ├── db/<name>-<hash>/                # one bare clone per repository URL
    └── checkouts/<name>-<hash>/<commit>/  # one checkout per commit
```

Set `QUIRE_HOME` to use another folder. Deleting the cache is always safe:
quire downloads what it needs again.

Once a locked commit is in the cache, quire doesn't use the network for it,
which is how `--offline` builds work.

## Concurrent runs

quire takes file locks, as Cargo does. One covers the cache, and one covers each
`target/<profile>` directory. Two builds or fetches at the same time wait for
each other (`Blocking waiting for file lock …`) instead of corrupting files.
Clones are written to a temporary folder and renamed into place, so an
interrupted clone never leaves a broken cache entry.
